synopsis: ISO/PAS 8800:2024 was published in December 2024 and tailors ISO 26262 for AI safety in road vehicles; its stated scope is road vehicles only, with several descriptions explicitly classified as vendor or on-road evidence [f2730, f2388, f2731, f15298]. For heavy off-road validation, the booklet uses its perception and assurance concepts as reference material: a team starting in October 2026 could realistically prepare a safety-case skeleton by mid-2027 alongside ISO 21815 and ISO 19014 mappings [f12069, f829]. It also identifies ISO/PAS 8800 as a source of assurance structures and as consistent with requiring validation and estimation data to be real or physically independent of the training-data generator, although that consistency claim is labelled independent on-road evidence and expert opinion [f655, f7101, f12264]. Acceptance of machine learning in safety functions remains disputed: one view excludes it in favour of certified deterministic sensors, while another accepts ISO/PAS 8800-style assurance [f1125, f12416]. There is also a terminology tension: one table calls the publication an international standard, whereas the glossary explicitly classifies it as a Publicly Available Specification, not a full standard, and describes the wider ML standardization effort as early and mostly unfinished [f2730, f15052, f15290].
